newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Bearish mood drives Slovak bourse down.
newsitem.headline: Bearish mood drives Slovak bourse down.

text.p: The two most heavily capitalised issues on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) - oil refiner Slovnaft and steel maker VSZ - declined in thinner trading on Wednesday, pulling the SAX index down 2.82 points to 189.38.
Brokers said the bearish mood on the Slovak market was in line with similar sentiment on neighbouring bourses and that the current downtrend was not expected to be reversed in the near future.
They said foreign investors seemed to be still waiting for further declines in order to buy at more attractive prices.

"If our expectations about the market's further downtrend are right, the decline will soon bring some very attractive prices which could accelerate foreign investors' activities," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
Slovnaft fell 49 crowns to 801, with the average price - used for calculating the index - down 5.76 percent.
VSZ lost 54 crowns to close at 550, with the average price easing 2.0 percent, and some brokers saying the price had now reached realistic levels.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta rose 90 crowns to 1,950, but dealers said the price had been pushed artificially high.
"Nafta's real price is well under 1,900 crowns, maybe at around 1,850 levels," Briska said.
Overall volume rose to 786,557 shares, boosted by direct trades, from 604,927 shares traded on Tuesday. Turnover increased to 389.78 million crowns, from 166.99 million.
